$comment: Machine-readable driver layer of tool-driver-cli-spec. A driver CLI first satisfies the pinned ai-native-cli-spec contract exactly (base/ai-native-cli-spec/contract.json): envelope keys, core error codes with their exit codes and retryable flags, self-description keys, pagination, batch and _untrusted. This file only adds what driving applications, application files and devices needs; it never redefines a base key, code or command. Prose: docs/LAYERING.md and docs/CORE-SPEC.md.

driver_profile.note: The base envelope keeps schema_version 1.0. A consumer recognizes a driver CLI by reference.driver_profile and context.driver_profile, never by extra envelope keys.

profiles.core: dry-run plan, confirm receipt, operation records
profiles.batch: base batch contract (items[] + summary) with a receipt or operation_id per dispatched item
profiles.query_page: base pagination with driver completeness fields in data

error_codes.note: Core codes come from the base contract unchanged. A driver CLI that emits one of these driver codes uses exactly this exit and retryable value; other product codes follow the base extension rules. The base E_TIMEOUT and E_INTERRUPTED are retryable, so a driver CLI uses them only when nothing was dispatched or nothing lasting happened; after dispatch an unobserved result is E_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN.

E_UNSUPPORTED.meaning: A valid request this build, mode or session cannot carry out; choose another capability.

E_BACKEND_UNAVAILABLE.meaning: The application, its service, plugin or device is absent, unreachable, unlicensed or speaks another protocol; nothing was dispatched.

E_PROTOCOL.meaning: The backend replied with something the CLI cannot read; read details.dispatch_state before any further write.

E_BUSY.meaning: The application main thread or the target is busy; nothing was dispatched; retry after a short wait.

E_NATIVE_FAILURE.meaning: The application rejected the operation and nothing lasting remained; read the receipt.

E_PARTIAL.meaning: Some requested stages or items took effect and others did not; read the receipt; never resend the whole request.

E_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN.meaning: The operation may have run and its result could not be established; query the operation and read back the target before anything else.

E_VERIFY_FAILED.meaning: The operation took effect and a required read-back check failed.

E_VERIFY_INCOMPLETE.meaning: The operation took effect and a required read-back check could not be completed.

E_HUMAN_REQUIRED.meaning: A person must act first: a dialog, a sign-in or licence prompt, an approval or a physical step. Relay details.action, wait, then run details.resume.

receipt_codes.note: Evaluate the rules in order against the receipt that a modifying call returns (data.receipt when ok is true, error.details.receipt when ok is false). The first rule whose conditions all hold decides ok and the allowed error codes.

conditions.unknown: execution, change, persistence or delivery is unknown
conditions.partial: change, persistence or delivery is partial
conditions.stopped: execution is failed, interrupted or not_started
conditions.lasting: change is applied, persistence is saved, delivery is delivered, or the receipt declares the artifact effect and lists an artifact this call produced
conditions.verification_missing: verification.status is incomplete, or change is applied and verification.status is not_run

error_details.note: A key written a|b needs one of the alternatives. Diagnostics name the failed constraint and the next step; they do not echo input values. Native messages copied into details are listed in details._untrusted.

control_flags.note: Driver CLIs add no global flag. Plan is the base --dry-run; apply and submit are the base --confirm <token>; dangerous commands also need the base --dangerous on both calls. --request-id and --idempotency-key keep their base meaning; a repeated key with the same content returns the original receipt with replayed: true and does not dispatch again, and the same key with different content is E_CONFLICT (idempotency_mismatch).

effects.write_type: A command is type write exactly when it has an effect other than observe; every write goes through --dry-run and --confirm. The base update command is the one exception (see exempt).

exempt.update: Base CLI-SPEC §14 self-update: a single command without --confirm and without a task scope. It changes the tool, not a target, so it is declared type write with effects [observe].

effects.tool_state: The tool's own records (operation store, confirm secret, update cache) are not targets and carry no effect. operation resolve is the only built-in that writes them and needs the scope that allowed the operation.

discovery.reference --index: one line per command: path, type, dangerous, description, effects, maturity; schema reference-index
discovery.reference --command <path>: one command with its schema entry, its error codes and the product JSON Schemas it names; schema reference-command

reference.public_schemas: Public driver schemas (urn:tool-driver-cli-spec:<name>:2.0) are referenced by identifier from the pinned specification and never inlined in a reference.

builtin_commands.operation show: read one operation record by --id: plan, status, receipt, resolution
builtin_commands.operation list: read recent operation records; --status filters, --limit bounds
builtin_commands.operation resolve: record what an independent read-back showed about an unknown or partial operation: --id, --outcome applied|not_applied|partial, --evidence; writes only the tool's own record, refuses while the operation is still running, needs the scope that allowed the operation

scope.env_var_rule: TOOL is the tool name upper-cased with '-' replaced by '_'
scope.written_by: a person, or an agent only when that person explicitly directs it; the CLI never creates or edits the file
scope.absent: read_only: only the observe effect is allowed

fields.roots: absolute directories whose files may be changed or saved
fields.outputs: absolute directories where new artifacts may be written
fields.destinations: prefixes of allowed delivery destinations, compared by URL scheme, host and whole path segments (local paths and file URIs as resolved paths); user info, queries, fragments and dot segments never match
fields.targets: optional selectors (engine_id, instance_id, object_id, locator_prefix); locator_prefix compares like destinations
fields.limits.max_operations: confirmed operations allowed under this scope, counted per scope_id for as long as the tool keeps its state

driver_sources: names of documents, objects, layers, features, components and nets
properties, annotations, notes, title-block and drawing text
native dialog, log and diagnostic messages

deviations.store_unavailable: Base CLI-SPEC §9 lets a tool degrade when its token store fails. A driver CLI refuses to dispatch instead (LAY-007): an unrecorded dispatch cannot be reconciled after a lost reply.
deviations.distribution: Base REPO-SPEC §4b npm shell is replaced by GitHub Release packaging and SkillHub distribution (LAY-008); actual install and upgrade paths still require validation.

long_operation_status.note: The base §16.2 names are kept; the driver layer only adds states.
